funds.name: Berkshire Hathaway
funds.note: One of the most useful funds to follow. Few positions, held for years, so a new buy is a real conviction call. Some stakes are kept confidential for a quarter and revealed later in an amendment.

funds.name: Duquesne Family Office
funds.note: Druckenmiller's personal money. Concentrated and opinionated, so new positions say a lot. He does trade quickly, so some moves may already be reversed by the time the filing appears.

funds.name: Pershing Square
funds.note: Holds about a dozen stocks for years. Every new position is a big bet, and Ackman usually explains it publicly. Also files fast 13D/Form 4 updates on big stakes.

funds.name: Appaloosa
funds.note: Strong long-term record. Fairly concentrated, but Tepper changes positioning quickly, so treat it as a view on sentiment as much as on single stocks.

funds.name: Baupost Group
funds.note: Classic value investor with a long record. The 13F shows only part of the fund (lots of private and credit deals), but stock buys are usually long-term.

funds.name: Himalaya Capital
funds.note: Charlie Munger's chosen manager. Only a handful of US positions, held for many years. Changes are rare, so when they happen they matter.

funds.name: Akre Capital
funds.note: One of the best long-term records among US funds. Buys high-quality compounders and rarely sells, so new names are worth a close look.

funds.name: Fundsmith
funds.note: UK manager popular with ISA investors. Low turnover quality stocks. Its 13F only covers US-listed holdings.

funds.name: Scion Asset Management
funds.note: Burry is famous and his filings make headlines, but the book is small, often heavy in put/call options, and turns over fast. Scion deregistered in late 2025, so there may be no new filings.

funds.name: Third Point
funds.note: Event-driven, so many positions are tied to a specific catalyst (spin-off, merger, activism). Useful for ideas, but holdings change fairly often.

funds.name: Viking Global
funds.note: Top 'Tiger cub' with a strong record. The 13F only shows longs, and turnover is moderate to high.

funds.name: Lone Pine Capital
funds.note: Growth-focused Tiger cub. Concentrated longs, moderate turnover. Shorts are not shown.

funds.name: Point72
funds.note: Dozens of separate trading teams, thousands of positions, and lots of hedging. Single moves tell you little. Look at big new positions only.

funds.name: Renaissance Technologies
funds.note: Trades by algorithm and holds thousands of stocks, so positions have usually changed long before the filing appears. Shown for interest, given little weight.

funds.name: Bridgewater Associates
funds.note: Much of the 13F is broad ETFs (S&P 500, emerging markets, gold), so it tells you more about its macro view than single-stock picks. Most US ETFs can't be bought by UK retail investors.

funds.name: Elliott Investment Mgmt
funds.note: The best-known activist fund. New stakes often come with a public campaign (and a 13D), which can move the share price.
